    late week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Tuesday)
Issued at 229 AM EDT Mon Sep 28 2026

Gradually warming temperatures and dry conditions will prevail 
across North and Central Georgia through mid-week. The deep mid-
level low that currently stretches across much of the East Coast 
(and was responsible for our recent false-Fall) will shift into 
the Northern Atlantic over the next few days, while a mid-level 
ridge builds across the Mississippi Valley. Very dry air (PWAT
values around 0.5") will linger over Georgia through mid-week, 
but the mid-level ridge nudging closer from the west will bring in
warmer temperatures. With mostly clear skies, light winds, and 
dewpoints in the upper 40s to low 50s, overnight low temperatures 
will radiationally cool to the low to mid 50s this morning, and
mid to upper 50s Tuesday morning. High temperatures will climb
from the low to mid 80s today, to the mid to upper 80s Tuesday
afternoon. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Tuesday night through Sunday)
Issued at 229 AM EDT Mon Sep 28 2026

Wednesday and Thursday will be the final days with essentially 
zero PoPs for the week ahead. Thursday and Friday will bring an 
amplifying a subtropical ridge over the Southeast and offshore 
over the western Atlantic. Meanwhile, moisture will increase as 
low-/mid- level flow off of the Gulf and Atlantic spreads inland. 
This setup will bring the return of isolated to scattered showers 
and storms Friday through Sunday. This synoptic pattern and AI NWP
Convective Hazard Forecasts from NCAR continue to lack a signal 
for severe weather potential. That said, the feed of tropical 
moisture could favor an increasing heavy rainfall threat, as 
ensemble guidance depicts PWAT reaching 1.8" to 2.0" over the 
weekend -- for context, the 90th percentile is 1.6". The 
increasing coverage of showers and storms will likely moderate 
temperatures over the weekend, evidenced by progged highs in the 
mid-70s to lower 80s.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 649 AM EDT Mon Sep 28 2026

VFR conditions through the period with only some high cirrus and 
fair wx afternoon CU. Winds light and variable across most of the
region. For the ATL area, winds light out of the NNW early this 
morning, trending NNE around 13Z, and then turning back NNW at 
5-8kts after around 18Z. Winds turn out of the east tonight into
Tuesday.

//ATL Confidence...12Z Update...

High for all elements.

Culver
